newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon adds $2 billion to submarine cost.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon adds $2 billion to submarine cost.

text.p: The Defence Department said Tuesday that a new plan for two shipyards instead of one to develop and build the Navy's next attack submarine added more than $2 billion to its estimated cost.

It said in a new quarterly report on major U.S. weapons costs that the cost of 30 of the attack submarines to be built beginning next year was estimated at the end of last year to be $67 billion, $2.1 more than previous estimates.
The new submarine is to be built jointly by General Dynamics' Electric Boat Division at Groton, Conn., and Newport News Shipbuilding and Drydock Co. in Virginia.

The Navy originally planned to have Electric Boat develop the submarine and then for the two shipyards to share construction of it. But Congress ordered the submarine to be developed and built by both shipyards.

In February, after the September-December 1996 quarter covered by the new report, the two companies went even further and announced they would cut costs with a plan backed by the Navy for each of them to build segments of the submarines and then assemble them at one of the yards.
